answer: Each epoch samples a fixed share of answers and sends them to a second panel drawn from separate subnetworks. A flagged answer is re-queued, not deleted, so the account keeps its record while its rewards vest across future epochs. That ordering puts the cost first: an island of clones pays the full audit price at every dawn and sees the lantern of payout only after months of clean work. Sampling 12% per epoch is enough because a farm cannot tell which of its answers will be drawn.
